newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE Albania envoy says date of visit still open.
newsitem.headline: OSCE Albania envoy says date of visit still open.

text.p: Franz Vranitsky, special envoy to Albania for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said on Thursday the exact timing of his planned fact-finding mission to Tirana remained open.

"I have had a telephone conversation with President Sali Berisha and we agreed that the OSCE mission will take place at the earliest possible moment. We have agreed to stay in contact," Vranitzky told a news conference at OSCE headquarters in Vienna.
Vranitzky said that the OSCE Troika of Swiss, Danish and Polish foreign ministers would travel to Tirana on Thursday to prepare his visit which he said should take place "in the next few days".
He said that Berisha had told him the situation in Albania was "very serious".
"I have no illusion that the mission is not going to be a very difficult one," he said. "We have to coordinate and harmonise rather than polarise."

The security body announced on Tuesday that former Austrian chancellor Vranitzky would travel to Albania as soon as possible to assess the situation in the troubled Balkan nation, where a state of emergency has been declared.

More than 20 people have been reported killed in Albania's south in violent protests, sparked by the collapse of several get-rich-quick investment schemes. A dusk-to-dawn curfew has been ordered and troops were called in to quell the unrest.

A delegation from the Council of Europe which promotes democracy and human rights is already in Albania, and a European Union mission headed by the Dutch foreign minister is due to arrive there on Friday.

The OSCE said Vranitzky's mission was to recommend action in order to "further the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms", to uphold the rule of law and initiate dialogue between all political forces in Albania.

The OSCE instructed Vranitzky to assure Berisha's government of its readiness to assist in resolving the crisis that has engulfed the country, "possibly in cooperation with other relevant international organisations".
